results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All other unit summaries match the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph; sections, order and unit counts agree.

results.quote: Four things could not be reached or confirmed.
results.finding: The spec paragraph names five unreachable items, including the 2023 Investor Day targets and share-price fall; the draft lists four (the Investor Day item is gone, consistent with the non-goals). The draft is the defensible version; the spec controlling idea is stale and should be reconciled.
The outliner marked no unit two_ideas; on reading, the dense p17 and p25 paragraphs still serve one controlling idea each.
Every body unit traces to S1-S5; the Mila/Larkfield paragraph (p03) and the failure-patterns callout trace to the role and the house format rather than a supporting claim, which the spec declares.

results.draft_locus: From an Acquiring License to Three Banking Permissions ¶3 (history table)
results.quote: | 2023 | EBITDA margin 46%, from 55% in 2022 | Release, 8 February 2024 |
results.finding: No sentence says what the dated-steps table shows. It follows a paragraph about the US and UK permissions and is followed by the margin paragraph; the reading the spec assigns it (check the order of construction at a glance) only appears in the INFERENCE block one paragraph later, and the table runs to October 2026 under a heading that ends in 2023 without saying why.
Other tables (acquisitions, figures, transfers), Figures 1-3 and quotations are followed or captioned by sentences that say what they show.
All other section and paragraph boundaries express their declared relationship.

results.quote: A **payout** is the transfer of a merchant's collected money to its bank account.
results.finding: Declared relationship is example: the payout ahead of settlement is the documented behavior that "control over funds" makes possible. The paragraph opens with a definition and never ties Sales day payout back to the licenses or control over funds, so the reader does not see why it is in the license section (flowB item 7 could not see the point of the paragraph).

results.draft_locus: July 2026 section end -> The Figures, With Their Definitions ¶1
results.quote: Four measures carry Adyen's reporting, and they are not interchangeable.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect: the acquisitions change headcount, margin guidance and capex in 2026, so the figures are read after them. The opening sentence makes no link to the acquisitions; the reason for the section's position is left implicit until the 399 acquired staff appear at the end of p30.

results.draft_locus: From an Acquiring License to Three Banking Permissions ¶4
results.quote: The run of additions has one visible stumble, in 2023. EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization
results.finding: Both readers stopped at the margin paragraph inside a history of permissions, saw EBITDA and net revenue defined twice, and objected to the margin and 2026 rows in a table under a heading ending in 2023. The placement is the spec's (the journal entry puts the margin fall in the history; the changelog records the flow rubric note not acted on).

results.quote: The third layer, Adyen's own infrastructure, has a price that Adyen reports.
results.finding: Both readers lost count of the three layers because the API paragraph sits between the statement of the layers and the third layer, and the second layer (licenses) gets no paragraph in this section. The order is the spec's (p12 before p13).

results.draft_locus: The Single-Platform Bet ¶3; The Engineering Record ¶1; Where the Evidence Stops
results.quote: Integrators see it as five named regions for live traffic
results.finding: Five live API regions and six named data-center regions are never distinguished; both readers suspected an inconsistency.

results.quote: It is also the reason Adyen gives for buying a loyalty engine.
results.finding: The forward pointer is never paid off: the acquisitions section quotes "will bridge this gap" without naming the gap or linking it to terminals or unified commerce. Both readers lost the thread.

results.quote: No page lists either per country.
results.finding: The coverage paragraph packs full-stack share, 14 connections, concentration risk, the UAE, France, Japan, Singapore and network memberships; "either" is ambiguous and both readers had to re-read to sort known from unknown.

results.quote: The in-house rule bends at the edge.
results.finding: "Edge" means the platform's product limit, the stateless acceptance layer and (apparently) the network perimeter; both readers could not tell which was meant in the last instance.

results.quote: The risk section says why:
results.finding: "Says why" promises a reason growth comes from existing customers; the quote explains why Adyen's share of each customer stays partial and why customers can leave. Both readers flagged the broken link.

results.quote: | Take rate | not used here | 15.5 bps | 17.0 bps | 16.2 bps | not given |
results.finding: "not used here", "not given" and "not reported" are unexplained; both readers wondered what was hidden.

results.quote: (K8 in [[meet-larkfield]])
results.finding: "K8" is an unexplained label for both readers.

results.quote: **Where we are in the payment's journey.** When Mila Janssen bought her €120.00 ten-class pass
results.finding: Both readers found the journey paragraph a dropped thread: Mila's payment is never used again, and the 2027 date jars with the 17 November 2026 cut-off stated a few lines later. Its presence and position are the spec's (p03; decision log keeps Larkfield to two appearances).

results.quote: 2023 and 2026 both show the margin moving with hiring while the platform stayed the same.
results.finding: The 2026 evidence is acquisition costs, acquired staff and a decision to "retain flexibility", not hiring in the 2023 sense; the 5,596-staff sentence sits after the guidance with no stated link. Both readers had to supply the connection.

results.quote: The largest customers pay the lowest rates, so losing volume from one of them lowers volume far more than revenue.
results.finding: The text never says the large customer reduced or left before drawing this conclusion; the merchant-mix and tiering quotes come between evidence and conclusion. Reported by flowA only.

results.quote: I cannot reconcile the two from public sources.
results.finding: The draft never says that the documentation presents Sales day payout as the standard model (the spec's open question), so an accelerated option beside a cautious default does not read as a contradiction. Reported by flowB only.

results.quote: then breadth on one platform, then the bank
results.finding: "Breadth on one platform" has no antecedent in the history, which covered licenses, listing and products. Reported by flowB only.

results.quote: In the audited notes it is a non-IFRS measure
results.finding: "It" means net revenue but follows two sentences about interchange and scheme fees. Reported by flowB only.

Both readers describe the declared organising principle (assertion-evidence-reasoning with a chronological history and a large-to-small run of layers) and mark no section position unclear; the failures above are local lost-thread points.

results.quote: "initiate payout of the Net Captured Volume to Merchant on the Payout Day, irrespective of whether the funds are actually received by Adyen from the Acquirer or Scheme Owner"
results.finding: "Sales day payout", "Net Captured Volume" and "Scheme Owner" arrive in a contract quotation with no gloss; the reader new to payments is not told that Sales day payout is an accelerated payout option or that the scheme owner is the card network.

Other payment terms (acquirer, credit institution, payout, merchant of record, interchange, scheme fees, take rate, basis points, sponsor bank, Interchange++, ARR, PSP, DDoS, EBITDA) are glossed at first use; full-stack is explicitly flagged as undefined by Adyen.
Established / depends / synthesis lists give the scoped, dated reading of the phrase and the customer and builder actions (plan separate systems, ask per country, take the accounting discipline).
The author's synthesis rewrites the architect's opening sentence with its scope and date.

The intro reader listed all eleven sections in the spec's order and named the annual report, press releases, audited figures and dated engineering material; it did not name shareholder letters/business updates or license and documentation pages, and was unsure what the engineering record consists of. Minor.
Sections predicted in exact order; source kinds mostly predicted (letters, updates and license/documentation pages missing).

Reader scopes the claim to payments, acquiring, terminals and banking; gives the 1 July 2026 closings with prices, the incubator model, multi-PSP, convergence with no date, Talon.One in the future tense, and the advice to plan for separate systems. Omits the 28 October "ongoing integration" wording and the point that no Adyen document says it abandoned building in-house; minor.

Reader gives 8% vs 21% excluding the unnamed customer, take rate 15.5 to 17.0 bps attributed to merchant mix, tiered pricing, and 16.2 bps in H1 2026 from volume tiering; net revenue definition only implied.
Reader lists the three practices, the three uncopyable assets with figures, and quotes Adyen's multi-provider risk statement.
